FR.name: France
FR.terroir_vibe: The spiritual home of fine wine, defined by AOC and strict adherence to traditional terroir heritage.

IT.name: Italy
IT.terroir_vibe: An ancient mosaic of indigenous varietals and alpine-to-coastal climates. Balance and high acidity are key.

ES.name: Spain
ES.terroir_vibe: High-altitude plateaus and Atlantic influence. Spain leads the world in organic vineyard area.

US.name: USA
US.terroir_vibe: Diversity from Pacific cooling to volcanic soils. A powerhouse of innovation and single-vineyard precision.

AR.name: Argentina
AR.terroir_vibe: High-altitude desert viticulture. Intense Andean sun creates concentrated, fruit-forward wines.

CL.name: Chile
CL.terroir_vibe: A climate island protected by the Andes and the Pacific. Famous for phylloxera-free own-rooted vines.

ZA.name: South Africa
ZA.terroir_vibe: Ancient granite soils meet cold Atlantic breezes. A bridge between Old World structure and New World fruit.

AU.name: Australia
AU.terroir_vibe: From ancient iron-rich soils to cool maritime climates. Shiraz is the national icon with unique power.

NZ.name: New Zealand
NZ.terroir_vibe: Cool climate and intense UV light create vibrant, aromatic profiles. The global benchmark for Sauvignon Blanc.

DE.name: Germany
DE.terroir_vibe: Steep slate slopes and river reflections. Home to the world's most elegant expressions of Riesling.

PT.name: Portugal
PT.terroir_vibe: A treasure trove of unique indigenous grapes. Famous for Port but rapidly becoming a dry wine destination.

AT.name: Austria
AT.terroir_vibe: Strict quality standards and focus on sustainable viticulture. Mineral-driven, structured, and elegant.

GR.name: Greece
GR.terroir_vibe: Volcanic soils and sea mist. Home to some of the world's most resilient and unique ancient grapes.

GE.name: Georgia
GE.terroir_vibe: The birthplace of wine. Famous for Qvevri (clay vessel) fermentation and 8,000 years of unbroken history.

HU.name: Hungary
HU.terroir_vibe: Volcanic hills and noble rot. The Tokaj region produces some of the world's finest dessert wines.

IL.name: Israel
IL.terroir_vibe: Ancient tradition meets modern tech. High-altitude vineyards in the Judean hills are producing world-class reds.

LB.name: Lebanon
LB.terroir_vibe: High-altitude plateau with 300 days of sun. A tiny but mighty producer with deep historic French influences.

CN.name: China
CN.terroir_vibe: The world's fastest-growing wine region. Ningxia's desert conditions produce powerful, Cabernet-style reds.

CA.name: Canada
CA.terroir_vibe: Extreme continental climate. Famous for Icewine but celebrated for elegant cool-climate reds.

MD.name: Moldova
MD.terroir_vibe: The highest density of vineyards per capita in the world. Deep limestone cellars and rich black soil.

RO.name: Romania
RO.terroir_vibe: A massive producer with high-quality karst limestone soils, echoing the terroir of Burgundy.

HR.name: Croatia
HR.terroir_vibe: The original home of Zinfandel. Dramatic limestone cliffs overlooking the Adriatic Sea.

SI.name: Slovenia
SI.terroir_vibe: The land of 'Orange Wine'. A leader in natural winemaking with high-altitude alpine influences.

CH.name: Switzerland
CH.terroir_vibe: Steep terraced vineyards and glacial influence. Almost all Swiss wine is consumed domestically.

UY.name: Uruguay
UY.terroir_vibe: Atlantic-influenced maritime climate. Tannat is the national signature grape, known for its structure.

MX.name: Mexico
MX.terroir_vibe: North America's oldest wine region. Arid Mediterranean climate tempered by Pacific breezes.

BR.name: Brazil
BR.terroir_vibe: The capital of South American sparkling wine. Basalt soils and high humidity create fresh, vibrant profiles.

TR.name: Turkey
TR.terroir_vibe: Over 800 indigenous grape varieties. A bridge between ancient civilization and modern quality.

MA.name: Morocco
MA.terroir_vibe: High-altitude vineyards in the Atlas Mountains. Surprisingly fresh, Mediterranean-style reds.

JP.name: Japan
JP.terroir_vibe: Volcanic soils and high rainfall. Koshu produces delicate, floral whites that pair perfectly with sushi.

AM.name: Armenia
AM.terroir_vibe: High-altitude volcanic soils. Home to the world's oldest known winery (Areni-1 cave).

CY.name: Cyprus
CY.terroir_vibe: Famous for Commandaria, the oldest named wine still in production. A phylloxera-free island.

BG.name: Bulgaria
BG.terroir_vibe: A historic producer with a focus on powerful, deep-colored reds from indigenous varietals.

RS.name: Serbia
RS.terroir_vibe: Resurgent tradition with a focus on Prokupac. Dramatic river-influenced microclimates.

PE.name: Peru
PE.terroir_vibe: Desert viticulture influenced by the Humboldt Current. Increasingly producing fine dry wines.

CO.name: Colombia
CO.terroir_vibe: High-altitude tropical viticulture. Unique 'double harvest' cycle due to equatorial conditions.

DO.name: Dominican Republic
DO.terroir_vibe: Commercial vineyards in the Caribbean. Tropical conditions produce unique, localized styles.

GB.name: United Kingdom
GB.terroir_vibe: Chalky soils similar to Champagne. Rapidly becoming a world-class destination for sparkling wine.

CH.name: Switzerland
CH.terroir_vibe: Alpine terraced vineyards with extreme slopes. Famous for mineral-driven Chasselas.

LU.name: Luxembourg
LU.terroir_vibe: Cool-climate white wines grown along the Moselle river, known for freshness and purity.

BE.name: Belgium
BE.terroir_vibe: Rising star in cool-climate viticulture, particularly successful with traditional method sparkling wines.

NL.name: Netherlands
NL.terroir_vibe: Focus on fungus-resistant (PIWI) varieties suitable for the maritime Dutch climate.

DK.name: Denmark
DK.terroir_vibe: One of the northernmost wine regions in the world, focused on aromatic white wines.

SE.name: Sweden
SE.terroir_vibe: Emerging region due to climate shifts, producing high-acid whites with distinct Nordic character.

TH.name: Thailand
TH.terroir_vibe: 'New Latitude' winegrowing. Tropical conditions require innovative double-pruning techniques.

IN.name: India
IN.terroir_vibe: High-altitude tropical viticulture. Nashik is the 'Wine Capital of India' with intense sun.
